serial.name: serial.init
serial.description:
serial.init(port, baud, rx, tx, opts?) -> bool
Open ONE port; becomes the active port for all other calls.
Opening again (any port) closes the previous one and releases its pins.
- port: 1 or 2 = hardware UART (UART0 is the console), 3 = RMT software UART
- baud: e.g. 115200, 921600 (port 3: 300-2000000)
- rx, tx: GPIO numbers (-1 = unused direction)
- opts: table {config="8N1", rxbuf=2048, txbuf=0, invert=false}

serial.name: serial.deinit
serial.description:
serial.deinit() -> bool
Flush TX, close the active UART and reset both pins to hi-Z GPIO.
Also runs automatically from C when the script exits.

serial.name: serial.is_initialized
serial.description:
serial.is_initialized() -> bool
True if a UART is currently open.

serial.name: serial.get_port
serial.description:
serial.get_port() -> 1|2|3|nil
Which port is active (nil = none).

serial.name: serial.set_pins
serial.description:
serial.set_pins(rx, tx) -> bool
Move the active UART to new pins on the fly (TX drained first).
The vacated pins are reset to hi-Z GPIO.

serial.name: serial.set_baud
serial.description:
serial.set_baud(baud) -> bool
Change baud rate live, without closing/reopening the port.

serial.name: serial.get_config
serial.description:
serial.get_config() -> table|nil
Active port info: {port=1, baud=115200, rx=18, tx=17, config="8N1", soft=false}.

serial.name: serial.get_stats
serial.description:
serial.get_stats() -> table|nil
Soft port (3) receive error counters since init: {rx_overflows, rx_frame_errors, rx_parity_errors}. nil for hardware ports.

serial.name: serial.write
serial.description:
serial.write(data) -> bytes_written
Binary-safe write (Lua strings may contain NULs). Pass ESP-NOW payloads straight through:
espnow.on_receive(function(mac, data) serial.write(data) end)

serial.name: serial.print
serial.description:
serial.print(value) -> bytes_written
Write value coerced to text (numbers/booleans ok), no newline.

serial.name: serial.println
serial.description:
serial.println(value?) -> bytes_written
Like serial.print plus "\r\n" (Arduino-style). No arg = just the newline.

serial.name: serial.flush
serial.description:
serial.flush()
Block until all queued TX bytes are on the wire.

serial.name: serial.available_for_write
serial.description:
serial.available_for_write() -> int
Bytes that can be written right now without blocking (TX backpressure check).

serial.name: serial.available
serial.description:
serial.available() -> int
Bytes waiting in the RX buffer.

serial.name: serial.read
serial.description:
serial.read(n?) -> string
Non-blocking: return up to n buffered bytes (default: all) as a binary string; "" if none.

serial.name: serial.read_until
serial.description:
serial.read_until(delim, max?) -> string|nil
Non-blocking framing: returns a complete chunk (delim stripped) once the 1-byte delimiter arrives, else nil while bytes accumulate internally. Accumulator capped at max (default 512) - overflow returns the blob as-is.

serial.name: serial.peek
serial.description:
serial.peek() -> int
Next buffered byte without consuming it, or -1 if the buffer is empty.

serial.name: serial.clear
serial.description:
serial.clear()
Discard everything in the RX buffer (and the read_until accumulator).

serial.name: serial.SOFT_PORT
serial.description:
serial.SOFT_PORT -> 3
Port number of the RMT software UART.

serial.name: serial.MAX_PORTS
serial.description:
serial.MAX_PORTS -> 3
Highest selectable port number.
